New Model from Mohammad

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(piCurve)
library(parallel)
library(lubridate)
library(glue)

rm(list = ls())
## original cleaned data from M
og_path <-  "/Users/Kathy/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-UW/Desktop/UW/projects/pe_curves/mohammad/data/cleaned-data/testData/pro_hourly_growth_par-cleaned-MA-Aug6-2026.csv"
# new data I generated 
time_res_tests <- c('15min', '30min', '1H')

# Initialize lists to save one data frame per time resolution.
df_renamed_list <- list()
df_label_list <- list()

# for loop to read in each time resolution
for (time_res in time_res_tests) {
  path <- glue(
    "/Users/Kathy/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-UW/Desktop/UW/projects/",
    "pe_curves/data/clean_growth_{time_res}.csv"
  )

  # Read and prepare data for one temporal resolution.
  df_main <- read.csv(path) |>
    rename(datetime = time) |>
    mutate(
      datetime = ymd_hms(datetime),
      time = format(datetime, "%H:%M:%S"),
      yr = year(datetime),
      mnth = month(datetime),
      dy = day(datetime)
    ) |>
    select(-X) |>
    group_by(cruise, cruise_day, pop) |>
    mutate(
      index_id = paste0("pi-", cur_group_id())
    ) |>
    ungroup()

  cat(
    "Time resolution: ", time_res,
    " | Total PI groups: ",
    n_distinct(df_main$index_id),
    "\n",
    sep = ""
  )

  # Keep the first 9 hours and rename PI-model columns.
  df_renamed <- df_main |>
    filter(hour <= 9) |>
    rename(
      P = slope,
      I = par_smooth
    ) |>
    mutate(
      time_res = time_res
    )

  # Save the full PI-model input data for this time resolution.
  df_renamed_list[[time_res]] <- df_renamed

  # Split data into one data frame per PI curve.
  df_sub <- df_renamed |>
    group_by(index_id) |>
    group_split()

  # Function to label P–I curve data type.
  modified_DataType_piCurve <- function(df) {
    tibble(
      data_type = DataType_piCurve(data = df)$data_type,
      index_id = unique(df$index_id)
    )
  }

  # Label each PI curve, then retain time-resolution metadata.
  df_label <- parallel::mclapply(
    df_sub,
    function(x) modified_DataType_piCurve(df = x),
    mc.cores = 13
  ) |>
    bind_rows() |>
    mutate(
      time_res = time_res
    )

  # Save labels for this time resolution.
  df_label_list[[time_res]] <- df_label
}

# Combine all time-resolution data frames after the loop.
df_renamed_all <- bind_rows(df_renamed_list)

# One row per index_id / PI curve, including data-type and time resolution.
df_label_all <- bind_rows(df_label_list)
```

helper function to add weights to low irradiance values
```{r}
upweight_low_light <- function(
  df,
  irradiance_col = "I",
  low_I_min = 0,
  low_I_max = 500,
  low_I_weight = 3
) {
  # Keep all observations once.
  df_weighted <- df

  # Identify observations to replicate.
  low_I_rows <- df |>
    filter(
      !is.na(.data[[irradiance_col]]),
      .data[[irradiance_col]] >= low_I_min,
      .data[[irradiance_col]] <= low_I_max
    )

  # Add extra copies. For weight = 3, each low-I observation appears 3 times total.
  if (nrow(low_I_rows) > 0 && low_I_weight > 1) {
    df_weighted <- bind_rows(
      df,
      low_I_rows[rep(seq_len(nrow(low_I_rows)), each = low_I_weight - 1), ]
    )
  }

  df_weighted
}
```

Run through original PI model
```{r}
# Lists to hold successful fit results and plot objects.
fit_par_list <- list()
pi_plot_data_list <- list()
weight <- 3

for (time_res_i in unique(df_renamed_all$time_res)) {

  message("Fitting curves for time resolution: ", time_res_i)

  df_time_res <- df_renamed_all |>
    filter(time_res == time_res_i)

  # Include time_res in grouping because index_id may repeat among files.
  df_sub <- df_time_res |>
    group_by(time_res, index_id) |>
    group_split()

  for (i in seq_along(df_sub)) {

    df <- df_sub[[i]]

    # Extract one value for each curve-level metadata field.
    index_id_i <- unique(df$index_id)[1]
    cruise_i <- unique(df$cruise)[1]
    cruise_day_i <- unique(df$cruise_day)[1]
    pop_i <- unique(df$pop)[1]

    if (nrow(df) <= 4) {
      message(
        "Skipping curve ", index_id_i,
        " at ", time_res_i,
        ": fewer than 5 rows"
      )
      next
    }

    tryCatch({
      # calculated with low light weighted values
      # Create a replicated version only for fitting and original df for plotting/metadata
      df_weighted <- upweight_low_light(
        df,
        irradiance_col = "I",
        low_I_min = 0,
        low_I_max = 250,
        low_I_weight = weight
      )
            
      fit <- Fit_piModel(
        data = df_weighted,
        STATapp = "MSE"
      )

      # Store fitted parameter results.
      fit_par_list[[length(fit_par_list) + 1]] <- tibble(
        time_res = time_res_i,
        index_id = index_id_i,
        cruise = cruise_i,
        cruise_day = cruise_day_i,
        pop = pop_i,
        n_obs = nrow(df),
        Pmax = unname(fit$par["Pmax"]),
        alpha = unname(fit$par["alpha"]),
        beta = unname(fit$par["beta"])
      )

      # Build the ggplot object.
      pi_plot <- Plot_piCurve(
        fit,
        df_weighted,
        length_out = 200,
        n_cores = 6
      ) +
        ggtitle(
        paste("Curve:", index_id_i)
        ) +
        theme(
          axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
          axis.title = element_text(size = 14)
        )

      # Save the plot and metadata together.
      pi_plot_data_list[[length(pi_plot_data_list) + 1]] <- list(
        plot = pi_plot,
        time_res = time_res_i,
        index_id = index_id_i,
        cruise = cruise_i,
        cruise_day = cruise_day_i,
        pop = pop_i
      )

    }, error = function(e) {
      message(
        "Skipping curve ", index_id_i,
        " at ", time_res_i,
        ": ", conditionMessage(e)
      )
    })
  }
}

# Combine fit results after all loops complete.
fit_par_all <- bind_rows(fit_par_list)
```

Save plots in a PDF
```{r}
library(patchwork)

fig_path <- "/Users/Kathy/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-UW/Desktop/UW/projects/pe_curves/figures/pi_curves"

# Convert saved plot objects and metadata into a tibble.
pi_plot_index <- tibble(
  plot = lapply(pi_plot_data_list, `[[`, "plot"),
  time_res = sapply(pi_plot_data_list, `[[`, "time_res"),
  index_id = sapply(pi_plot_data_list, `[[`, "index_id"),
  cruise = sapply(pi_plot_data_list, `[[`, "cruise"),
  cruise_day = sapply(pi_plot_data_list, `[[`, "cruise_day"),
  pop = sapply(pi_plot_data_list, `[[`, "pop")
)

output_dir <- fig_path
dir.create(output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

for (pop_i in unique(pi_plot_index$pop)) {
  for (time_res_i in unique(pi_plot_index$time_res)) {

    # Filter to one population and one time resolution.
    pop_time_plots <- pi_plot_index |>
      filter(
        pop == pop_i,
        time_res == time_res_i
      )

    # Do not make an empty PDF.
    if (nrow(pop_time_plots) == 0) {
      next
    }

    # Make population name safe for file names.
    pop_file_name <- gsub(
      pattern = "[^A-Za-z0-9_-]",
      replacement = "_",
      x = as.character(pop_i)
    )

    # Example: PI_curves_pro_3min.pdf
    pdf_file <- paste0(
      "PI_curves_",
      pop_file_name,
      "_",
      time_res_i,
      "weight",
      weight,
      ".pdf"
    )

    pdf(
      file = file.path(output_dir, pdf_file),
      width = 14,
      height = 9,
      onefile = TRUE
    )

    # Each cruise becomes a separate page in the PDF.
    for (cruise_i in unique(pop_time_plots$cruise)) {

      cruise_plots <- pop_time_plots |>
        filter(cruise == cruise_i) |>
        arrange(cruise_day)

      # One panel per cruise day.
      page_plot <- wrap_plots(
        cruise_plots$plot,
        ncol = 4
      ) +
        plot_annotation(
          title = paste(
            "P–I curves | Population:", pop_i,
            "| Resolution:", time_res_i,
            "| Cruise:", cruise_i
          ),
          subtitle = "Each panel represents one cruise day"
        ) &
        theme(
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
          axis.text = element_text(size = 9),
          axis.title = element_text(size = 10)
        )

      print(page_plot)
    }

    dev.off()

    message(
      "Saved PDF: ",
      file.path(output_dir, pdf_file)
    )
  }
}
```

```{r}
library(tidyr)
fit_par_long <- fit_par_all %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Pmax, alpha, beta),
    names_to = "parameter",
    values_to = "estimate"
  ) %>%
  filter(is.finite(estimate)) %>%
  mutate(
    time_res = factor(
      time_res,
      levels = c("3min", "15min", "30min", "1H")
    ),
    parameter = factor(
      parameter,
      levels = c("Pmax", "alpha", "beta")
    )
  )

# log normalize
fit_par_log_long <- fit_par_long %>%
  filter(
    parameter %in% c("Pmax", "alpha", "beta"),
    estimate > 0
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    log_estimate = log(estimate)
  )

# Calculate Tukey outlier thresholds separately for each
# time-resolution × parameter distribution.
outlier_limits <- fit_par_log_long %>%
  group_by(time_res, parameter) %>%
  summarise(
    q1 = quantile(log_estimate, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3 = quantile(log_estimate, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr = IQR(log_estimate, na.rm = TRUE),
    lower_limit = q1 - 1.5 * iqr,
    upper_limit = q3 + 1.5 * iqr,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Create a plot-only data frame without Tukey outliers.
fit_par_plot <- fit_par_log_long %>%
  left_join(
    outlier_limits,
    by = c("time_res", "parameter")
  ) %>%
  filter(
    log_estimate >= lower_limit,
    log_estimate <= upper_limit
  ) %>%
  select(
    -q1,
    -q3,
    -iqr,
    -lower_limit,
    -upper_limit
  )

ggplot(
  fit_par_log_long,
  aes(x = parameter, y = log_estimate, fill = parameter)
) +
  geom_violin(
    trim = FALSE,
    alpha = 0.55,
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.16,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    fill = "white",
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    aes(color = parameter),
    width = 0.10,
    height = 0,
    alpha = 0.35,
    size = 1.4,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_grid(
    rows = vars(parameter),
    cols = vars(time_res),
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Pmax" = "#1B9E77",
      "alpha" = "#7570B3",
      "beta" = "#D95F02"
    ),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Pmax" = "#1B9E77",
      "alpha" = "#7570B3",
      "beta" = "#D95F02"
    ),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "P–I curve parameter distributions across time resolutions",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Fitted parameter value"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", color = NA),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = grid::unit(0.8, "lines")
  )
```

```{r}
# functions
fit_2tanh_model <- function(x) {
  fit_noDR <- Fit_piModel(data = x, Control = list(maxit = 5000))
  
  fit <- Fit_piModel(
    data = x,
    DarkReactionRate_R = T,
    Control = list(maxit = 5000)
  )
  
  
  tidy_output <-
    function(model, data = x) {
      params <- model$par
      mse <- model$value
      sqa <- model$SQA
      
      c(index_id = unique(x$index_id),
        params,
        mse = mse,
        sqa)
    }
  
  if (fit_noDR$SQA["R2"] >= fit$SQA["R2adj"]) {
    tidy_output(model = fit_noDR)
  } else{
    tidy_output(model = fit)
  }
}
```
